summary: Tonight's run consolidates 167 clusters (selected 35) spanning DAN, AMO, ZEC, NUM, EZK, and ECC. The dominant learning is eight generalizable improvements: (1) figs-activepassive ATs should name God explicitly when the divine agent is clear and offer a second AT option when one is too narrow; (2) Aramaic emphatic-pronoun constructions warrant their own writing-pronouns note distinct from antecedent-ambiguity; (3) translate-symaction notes should always accompany ANE court regalia (purple garments, gold chains) and profane sacred-vessel use; (4) translate-names notes must identify who the referent IS, not just their grammatical category; (5) figs-idiom notes must be dropped when figs-metaphor or figs-doublet already covers the same phrase; (6) chapter intros require a numbered structural outline with verse-range markers; and two DAN book-scoped rules about the Aramaic idioms כָּל קֳבֵל דִּי and כְּעַן.

Tonight's consolidation covers five new TN note-category patterns not yet in memory (figs-idiom, translate-symaction, translate-names, writing-quotations, figs-infostructure) drawn from general-tier signals across DAN/AMO/ZEC/EZK/ECC, plus one strengthen of the existing figs-activepassive entry on preferred agent phrasing in active-voice ATs, and one book-scoped note on a recurring DAN Aramaic idiom. Single-editor book-scoped and situational clusters are conservatively held.

Consolidated 35 selected clusters (DAN, AMO, ZEC, EZK, NUM, 1CH, ECC, MIC) spanning 169 total clusters. Five generalizable rules emerged: editors added stable translate-symaction notes in narrative prose; reworked translate-names boilerplate to add identity context; dropped image-based figs-idiom notes and reclassified them as figs-metaphor or figs-metonymy; dropped trivially-obvious metonymy notes; and consistently expanded chapter intros with numbered verse-range outlines.

summary: Tonight's consolidation surfaces six generalizable rules from 169 clusters: (1) figs-activepassive alternate translations should name the explicit agent rather than staying passive; (2) 'behold' (hinneh/וְהִנֵּה) is writing-foreground, not figs-metaphor — editors dropped metaphor tags and added foreground tags across DAN and AMO; (3) translate-symaction notes are expected for royal regalia (purple garments, gold chains) and sacred-vessel drinking scenes; (4) translate-names notes must go beyond 'X is the name of a man' and include relationship or meaning; (5) obviously self-evident figs-metonymy should be dropped rather than annotated; (6) writing-pronouns notes should be added whenever a verse has a pronoun chain with ambiguous referents across 3+ books.

summary: Tonight's run surfaced 35+ clusters dominated by DAN/AMO/ZEC TN work from justplainjane47, bethoakes, and deferredreward. Four actionable general patterns emerge that are not yet in memory: (1) editors consistently add translate-symaction notes for culturally opaque symbolic actions; (2) editors expand figs-idiom alternate translations to offer multiple options rather than one; (3) editors enrich translate-names notes beyond bare 'is the name of' to supply identifying context; and (4) when converting divine-passive alternates to active form, editors name the agent explicitly. One book-scoped DAN pattern is also worth recording: the Aramaic idiom כָּל־קֳבֵל recurs across five chapters with consistent idiom notes.

Tonight's run consolidated 32 general-tier and book-scoped clusters from DAN, AMO, ZEC, ECC, NUM, EZK, and 1CH editor signals. Four new rules were identified that are not yet in existing memory: (1) translate-names notes should explain name significance rather than merely labeling 'name of a man'; (2) writing-pronouns notes should be added when an author states a pronoun explicitly alongside a verb that already encodes it (emphatic usage), a sub-type distinct from ambiguous reference; (3) figs-activepassive alternate translations should always include at least one named-agent option; (4) chapter introductions should use numbered structural outlines rather than prose-paragraph summaries. One existing rule was also strengthened: figs-idiom notes should be dropped when the idiom's meaning is transparent or already inferable from immediate context.

Tonight's consolidation surfaces three generalizable signals from 169 candidate clusters (DAN, AMO, ZEC, ECC, NUM, EZK editors). First: editors in DAN+AMO systematically improve active-passive alternate translations by naming the actor explicitly (God / someone) rather than leaving agent-vague restatements. Second: editors across ZEC, DAN, and ECC enrich bare 'the name of a man/place' notes with role and cultural context. Third: the existing translate-symaction 'trim' guidance (derived from LAM+HAB poetry) is too cautious for narrative prose — editors consistently add notes for two high-significance categories in DAN+AMO. Situational and single-editor clusters (DAN Aramaic idiom כָּל-קֳבֵל; DAN-only writing-foreground; single-chapter figs-abstractnouns) were not proposed.
